channel.title: NBC Sports Rotoworld NFL Player News
channel.description: Unofficial personal Rotoworld NFL player-news feed.

item.title: Alex Highsmith (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Alex Highsmith PIT Linebacker

Highsmith suffered an ankle injury in Week 11 and starts out the week not practicing. He was wearing an ankle brace in the team facility on Tuesday and head coach Mike McCarthy said it will be “tough” for Highsmith to play in a shortened Week 12 where the Steelers play the Broncos on Friday. Highsmith is trending in the wrong direction this week, but his ankle issue does not seem to be a major injury.

item.title: Quinyon Mitchell (hamstring) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
item.description:
Quinyon Mitchell PHI Cornerback

Eagles DC Vic Fangio said today he believed Mitchell would be able to go, and it seems like he’s trending in the right direction after hitting the practice field today. It would certainly help anyone facing CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens out this week if Mitchell were able to go.

item.title: Dallas Goedert (shin) practiced in full on Tuesday.
item.description:
Dallas Goedert PHI Tight End

That makes us feel pretty confident that he’ll suit up for Thanksgiving’s game against the Cowboys after a limited session on Monday. The Eagles’ passing game is in pretty rough shape with Joe Milton under center, but Dallas’ issues invite a TE1-capable game script for Goedert if the Eagles can take advantage of it.

item.title: Will Shipley (foot/illness) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
item.description:
Will Shipley PHI Running Back

With the news that Saquon Barkley is practicing in full, Shipley’s waiver wire appeal has downgraded drastically. He’s a reasonable stash and little more at this point in 12-team leagues.

item.title: Saquon Barkley (neck/illness) practiced in full on Tuesday.
item.description:
Saquon Barkley PHI Running Back

It’s an upgrade over his limited session on Monday. Barkley told reporters after Sunday’s game that he doesn’t think he’ll ever get to 100 percent again for the rest of the season, saying “That’s not how football works.” But it seems like he’s at least “football healthy” enough to go against the Cowboys on Thanksgiving.

item.title: Pat Bryant (ankle) is practicing in full for Denver’s Week 12 game against the Steelers.
item.description:
Pat Bryant DEN Wide Receiver

Bryant survived an injury scare on Sunday and this confirms that he should be in a good place to play on Friday. He took over as Denver’s No. 2 receiver against the Raiders, out-targeting Courtland Sutton 4-2, but wasn’t able to make much fantasy hay of the increased workload. Pittsburgh should be another game that mostly sees Bryant as a FLEX play at best.

item.title: Free agent WR Brandon Aiyuk will visit the Commanders on Wednesday.
item.description:
Brandon Aiyuk

Aiyuk’s last two days have gone pretty much exactly what you would have expected after the 49ers finally released him. He’ll likely sign with the Commanders practice squad officially tomorrow.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Broncos designated Tyler Badie (thumb) to return from injured reserve.
item.description:
Tyler Badie DEN Running Back

His 21-day window opens with a full practice. Seems like perhaps J.K. Dobbins’ suspension has accelerated the timeline on this decision, so Badie may have a chance to be activated for Friday’s game against the Steelers.

item.title: Roschon Johnson (ankle) did not practice on Tuesday.
item.description:
Roschon Johnson CHI Running Back

We wouldn’t be surprised if he was an IR candidate after he was carted off during Week 11’s win over the Saints. Salvon Ahmed will likely take over third-string duties for the Bears.

item.title: Sam LaPorta (ankle) practiced in full on Tuesday.
item.description:
Sam LaPorta DET Tight End

LaPorta profiles as a TE1 option in a game with a juicy 55.5 over/under on Thanksgiving. This full session should assure that he skips the questionable line and proceeds directly to a fun game script in the early window.

item.title: Christian Benford (groin) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
item.description:
Christian Benford BUF Cornerback

It’s his first practice since suffering the groin injury in Week 10. We had a feeling the Bills would do all they could to have the full roster ready for the Chiefs and it appears Benford will indeed have a chance to suit up.

item.title: Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
item.description:
Dalton Kincaid BUF Tight End

Kincaid talked to reporters after practice and said he is “most likely” playing on Thanksgiving. Not a surprise after a pair of limited sessions, it seems like the Bills simply used their Week 11 game against the Dolphins as an exhibition to rest Kincaid ahead of the Chiefs game. He’ll be on the TE1 line if, as expected, he goes.

Source: Matt Parrino

item.title: Brandon Aiyuk cleared waivers on Tuesday, making him a free agent.
item.description:
Brandon Aiyuk

Nobody claimed his 49ers contract. Our next blurb on Aiyuk will probably read something like “Commanders signed WR Brandon Aiyuk,” but until then we’re legally obligated to note that Adam Schefter reported he is expected to draw interest from “a few teams.”

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Bears claimed CB Isaac Yiadom off waivers from the Commanders.
item.description:
Isaac Yiadom CHI Cornerback

Yiadom has been a decent depth corner for most of the last half-decade, but only played on special teams with the Commanders this year. Perhaps the Bears see more in him, or perhaps they just need a gunner.

item.title: Broncos coach Sean Payton said he suspended J.K. Dobbins one game for conduct detrimental to the team.
item.description:
J.K. Dobbins DEN Running Back

For those of you who haven’t had the pleasure of rostering Dobbins anywhere, know that he played just one snap on Sunday. Whatever went down almost certainly has something to do with that low snap count, though Payton wouldn’t get into it publicly with reporters. If Dobbins could agitate enough to get released, maybe we’d get somewhere in fantasy circles, but as it stands there’s no reason to hold him in shallow leagues.

Source: Nick Kosmider

item.title: Kenneth Walker (groin) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
item.description:
Kenneth Walker KC Running Back

This is at least the start of a movement for Walker to be active for Thanksgiving’s game against the Bills, it’s his first practice since suffering the groin injury. His status on Wednesday will be one of the biggest fantasy storylines of the week as it also underscores whether Emmett Johnson will be an RB1 or a contingency FLEX play. It’s hard to read too much into this one way or another, with Andy Reid saying early today that Walker “feels good” probably the best bellwether we have at this point.

item.title: Jake Ferguson did not practice on Tuesday.
item.description:
Jake Ferguson DAL Tight End

He will almost certainly miss the Thanksgiving game against the Eagles after two more missed practices. It is perhaps feasible he could return for Week 13, which would be his fourth week since suffering this new knee injury.

item.title: Ben Skowronek (calf) did not practice on Tuesday.
item.description:
Ben Skowronek PIT Wide Receiver

This could open up more snaps for Pittsburgh’s ancillary receivers even if Skowronek is no fantasy force. He played 10 and 17 snaps in his first two weeks back from the calf injury after he was active for Week 10.

item.title: Michael Pittman (foot) practiced in full on Tuesday.
item.description:
Michael Pittman PIT Wide Receiver

Mike McCarthy has said he is “very confident” that Pittman will play in Week 12 and this listing does little to douse that. It’s hard to understand if Pittman’s return will actually make Aaron Rodgers target the middle of the field or not, but he would be a rough FLEX play either way in his first game off IR with all 32 teams playing in Week 12.

item.title: Colts signed QB Shane Buechele off the Bills’ practice squad.
item.description:
Shane Buechele IND Quarterback

Buechele got his first NFL experience last year in Week 18, at age 27, when he completed 7-of-14 passes for 88 yards in a game the Chiefs were (probably) looking to lose against the Raiders. He was sacked five times. These last six Colts games will feel like they take five months.

item.title: Ravens waived WR LaJohntay Wester.
item.description:
LaJohntay Wester BAL Wide Receiver

Wester muffed two punts last week against the Panthers, which we’re told is “not a good way to keep your roster spot” when you are here to be the returner. The Ravens will shuffle the deck here.

Source: Jeff Zrebiec

item.title: Packers activated Micah Parsons (knee/PUP) off the physically unable to perform list.
item.description:
Micah Parsons GB Defensive End

In other words, the questionable listing from an hour ago does not actually matter. Parsons is back after losing almost a year to a torn ACL. He’ll be directed to put some havoc on the field in his return against the Rams on Wednesday night.

item.title: Steve Avila (hamstring) will not play in Los Angeles’ Week 12 game against the Packers.
item.description:
Steve Avila

Avila did not play in Week 10 and did not practice at all this week coming out of a Week 11 bye. Perhaps the extra rest after this one will get him to a workable place in Week 13. Beaux Limmer started at guard in his place against the Cardinals in Week 10, but with Coleman Shelton (hamstring) also ruled out at center it’s possible that Limmer starts there instead. Bill Murray is the only other interior lineman on the 53-man roster currently, and it’s going to be almost Thanksgiving, not Groundhog Day.

item.title: Colby Parkinson (ribs) is not on Los Angeles’ final Week 11 injury report.
item.description:
Colby Parkinson

He and Tyler Higbee will both be featured parts of this offense as the Rams look to get by without Puka Nacua. The one that catches a touchdown will be the one that you don’t start.

item.title: Kyren Williams (toe) is not on Los Angeles’ final Week 12 injury report.
item.description:
Kyren Williams

He’ll be good to go against the Packers on Wednesday night. Williams should figure into the high RB2 mix as the Rams try to replace Puka Nacua once again with plenty of split back formations.

item.title: Colts signed OL Wanya Morris off the Cowboys’ practice squad.
item.description:
Wanya Morris IND OFFENSIVE TACKLE (SUB)

Jalen Travis and Bernhard Raimann are both dealing with injuries, and other names on the Colts 53-man roster at tackle include Luke Tenuta, Charlie Heck, and Matt Goncalves (a guard last year) as they try to see out the end of this disastrous season. Morris will attempt to see it with them.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Micah Parsons (knee) is questionable for Green Bay’s Week 12 game against the Rams.
item.description:
Micah Parsons GB Defensive End

We have no doubts he’ll play — Rams EDGE Myles Garrett said he was able to give Parsons some tickets for the 27-year-old’s long-awaited return yesterday. But players returning from PUP and IR have frequently just gotten a questionable tag regardless of how likely they are to play. Parsons got in limited work in each of the three practices this week.

item.title: Josh Jacobs (thumb) is questionable for Green Bay’s Week 11 game against the Rams.
item.description:
Josh Jacobs GB Running Back

He got in limited work in each of Green Bay’s three practices this week, though some of them were “estimated” given the short week. Matt LaFleur said he was unlikely to play on Monday, so perhaps this is just a gamesmanship questionable. Obviously, if Jacobs does play, he’d be a suitable low-end RB2.

item.title: Ravens waived QB Kedon Slovis.
item.description:
Kedon Slovis

He’ll reportedly garner interest from the Arizona Cardinals for some reason. Slovis, 25, played for Arizona in the preseason and the Texans in the 2025 preseason. Over his three preseason stints he’s 86-of-126 for 816 yards, three touchdowns, and three interceptions while taking nine sacks.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh, asked about feeding Omarion Hampton more, said “in hindsight, we should have done that sooner.”
item.description:
Omarion Hampton LAC Running Back

Many cases of fantasy managers who drafted Hampton in the first two rounds this past August nodding fervently at this news have been reported. Hampton had 15 touches last week and 23 against the Ravens in Week 10. With Justin Herbert (concussion protocol) uncertain for Week 12, it looks like Hampton will be a major part of the game plan yet again against the Patriots.

Source: ProFootballTalk at NBCSports.com

item.title: Browns designated RB Raheim Sanders (hip) to return from injured reserve.
item.description:
Raheim Sanders CLE Running Back

His 21-day window will open today. Sanders probably won’t come back to a real role unless there are injuries ahead of him, but perhaps he’ll cut into Dylan Sampson’s No. 2 role and make both of them unrosterable.

item.title: Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said Ken Walker (ankle) will participate in practice Tuesday.
item.description:
Kenneth Walker KC Running Back

“I’m not anticipating a ton of work,” Reid said of Walker, who has missed two straight games and did not practice Monday ahead of the team’s Thanksgiving matchup against Buffalo. “Let’s see how does. He’s feeling pretty good.” If he practices today and Wednesday, Walker should be active for Thursday night. The Chiefs have committed to Walker as the team’s lead back despite Emmett Johnson putting up elite numbers in his absence. Johnson would be startable only in deeper fantasy leagues if Walker is good to go for Thursday.

Source: Nate Taylor

item.title: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports Greg Newsome (ankle) will miss 4-6 weeks.
item.description:
Greg Newsome NYG Cornerback

He’s headed to injured reserve. Newsome will undergo surgery after sustaining a high ankle sprain in Week 11. His absence could be a blow to a Giants secondary that has played well in 2026, allowing the NFL’s 12th lowest drop back success rate and 11th lowest drop back EPA. Newsome through Week 11 had allowed the lowest EPA per target of any Giants cornerback.

Source: Jordan Schultz

item.title: The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette’s Gerry Dulac reports DK Metcalf could face fines from the NFL following his Week 11 ejection.
item.description:
DK Metcalf PIT Wide Receiver

Metcalf won’t be suspended for his repeated fights with Eagles defenders on Sunday but he could be fined for the behavior. Metcalf’s meltdown came after he had one catch for two yards in the first half. Among the most inefficient wide receivers in the game, Metcalf has had a disappointing 2026 campaign as the team’s No. 1 wideout. He’ll profile as a flex option in Week 12 against a Broncos defense allowing the fourth fewest fantasy points per target to boundary wideouts.

Source: Gerry Dulac

item.title: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald would not say if Sam Darnold (oblique) would start in Week 12.
item.description:
Sam Darnold SEA Quarterback

Darnold was able to return to practice on Monday ahead of the Seahawks’ Week 12 game against the division rival Niners. Macdonald suggested he wouldn’t make a call on a starting quarterback before Wednesday though. “I think before making any declarations with Sam, we’ll get through Wednesday, see how Wednesday goes,” Macdonald said. “So nothing official yet. He was able to train a little bit here, do some rehab here, he also was able to get away. He’s optimistic, but I think with today’s practice cadence and speed of today, it’s probably wise to wait to make any declarations until we get through Wednesday’s practice.” Drew Lock, the most efficient quarterback in the NFL this season, could get another start if Darnold isn’t quite ready. It’s an excellent matchup against a 49ers defense that profiles as a pass funnel.

Source: Pro Football Talk

item.title: Treylon Burks caught 2-of-3 targets for 30 yards in the Commanders’ Week 11 win over the Bengals.
item.description:
Treylon Burks WAS Wide Receiver

While Burks did little in the box score, he drew a defensive pass interference call in the end zone that set up the team’s only touchdown of the game on a Jacory Croskey-Merritt touchdown run on the following play. his three targets finished tied for fourth on the team behind Antonio Williams’ 12, Stefon Diggs’ six, and Chig Okonkwo’s five, leaving Burks in shaky fantasy territory as the team enters the final two months of play.

item.title: Stefon Diggs caught 4-of-6 targets for 45 yards in the Commanders’ Week 11 win over the Bengals.
item.description:
Stefon Diggs WAS Wide Receiver

Diggs was shown displaying clear frustration on multiple occasions, the two most glaring of which came on the sideline following a poorly thrown ball from quarterback Jayden Daniels. History would repeat in the second half when Daniels bounced a ball to Diggs in the end zone after escaping to his right, the former of whom had broken free of coverage over the middle of the field. Diggs’ veteran presence will need to persist through the uneven quarterback play if the Commanders are to make a push toward the postseason during the final two months of play, a road that was made that much easier with the walk off win over the Bengals. Up next are the downtrodden Cardinals in Week 12, where Diggs will remain a viable Flex play in fantasy.

item.title: Chig Okonkwo caught 4-of-5 targets for 66 yards in the Commanders’ Week 11 win over the Bengals.
item.description:
Chig Okonkwo WAS Tight End

The veteran tight end’s five targets finished third on the team behind the 11 of Antonio Williams and six of veteran Stefon Diggs. Okonkwo remains unlikely to return elite volume in the more conservative Washington offense but can continue to return usable fantasy outings as a viable TE2. He’ll push for TE1 status in a plus matchup against the Cardinals in Week 12.

item.title: Antonio Williams caught 9-of-11 targets for 122 yards in the Commanders’ Week 11 win over the Bengals.
item.description:
Antonio Williams WAS Wide Receiver

Williams was the top option for quarterback Jayden Daniels throughout, seeing consistent volume throughout. He staked his mark on the game for good with a 42-yard reception to set up the game-winning field goal as time expired, effectively saving the Commanders’ season in the process. After teasing fantasy upside throughout the first half of his rookie season, Williams finally appears to have earned the top role through the air as he enters the final two months of the regular season as a viable WR3 with WR2 upside in fantasy circles. He gets a tantalizing matchup against the Cardinals in Week 12.

item.title: Austin Ekeler rushed seven times for 41 yards in the Commanders’ Week 11 win over the Bengals, adding three yards on two receptions.
item.description:
Austin Ekeler WAS Running Back

The box score does little to jump off the page but it is notable that Ekeler played over Rachaad White as the primary change of pace option behind Jacory Croskey-Merritt. Whether that was due to White’s presence on the injury report throughout the week remains to be seen. Either way, the only fantasy-viable back currently on the roster appears to be Croskey-Merritt, leaving both Ekeler and White of little value moving forward.

item.title: Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed 13 times for 54 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 11 win over the Bengals, adding 23 yards on two receptions.
item.description:
Jacory Croskey-Merritt WAS Running Back

Croskey-Merritt immediately returned from injured reserve to handily lead the team in snaps and opportunities, despite veteran Austin Ekeler playing the team’s first series. More interesting was the fact that Rachaad White hardly had a role, with Ekeler serving as the primary change of pace option, something that could be due to White’s presence on the injury report throughout the week. Either way, Croskey-Merritt appears to have a stranglehold on lead duties moving forward, a role that keeps him as a viable RB2 in the immediate future. That holds true for a Week 12 meeting with the Cardinals.

item.title: Jayden Daniels completed 23-of-35 passes for 289 yards in the Commanders’ 22-20, Week 11 win over the Bengals, adding 55 yards on six carries.
item.description:
Jayden Daniels WAS Quarterback

Daniels and the Commanders were unable to get anything going offensively while playing through driving rain in the first half, going three-and-out on three of their first four possessions before their lone touchdown drive of the game on their final possessions before the break. Things would change in the second half as Daniels led five consecutive scoring drives, all of which ended in field goals, proving enough to eek out a victory that could have saved the team’s season. The 4-5-1 Commanders remain two games behind the division-leading Giants with two months remaining in the regular season, but a loss to the Bengals would have made a late-season push toward the playoffs almost insurmountable. Daniels and the Commanders now prepare to face the Cardinals on the road in Week 12, where the veteran signal caller will remain an upside QB2.

item.title: Ja’Marr Chase caught 5-of-9 targets for 31 yards in the Bengals’ Week 11 loss to the Commanders.
item.description:
Ja'Marr Chase CIN Wide Receiver

The two teams played to a scoreless first frame through driving rain in Maryland, with Chase appearing to come alive on the teams first possession of the second quarter. He would ultimately be locked up by sticky coverage heavily influenced by Washington’s ability to generate consistent pressure, narrowly missing a downfield shot in the second half in triple coverage that could have propelled his fantasy day toward a usable week. Chase’s next opportunity to flourish comes in a Week 12 meeting with the Saints, where his skillset sets up well to take advantage of one of the highest single-high rates in the league.

item.title: Tee Higgins caught 2-of-3 targets for 43 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 11 loss to the Commanders.
item.description:
Tee Higgins CIN Wide Receiver

Higgins got in the box score with a 31-yard touchdown reception late in the second quarter after the two teams played to a scoreless first frame in driving rain. The Bengals did not alter their typical pass-heavy ways despite the rain throughout the first half, with Higgins seeing modest volume while primarily matched up against Rasul Douglas on the perimeter. Joe Burrow fed the running backs and tight ends a massive 24 targets in the face of unrelenting pressure from the Commanders, a situation likely to correct against the single-high-heavy Saints in Week 12, where Higgins returns to WR2 status in fantasy.

item.title: Mike Gesicki caught 5-of-6 targets for 77 yards in the Bengals’ Week 11 loss to the Commanders.
item.description:
Mike Gesicki CIN Tight End

Gesicki saw increased usage against an aggressive Commanders team that brought consistent pressure into the backfield, with the highlight of his game coming on a 32-yard reception over the middle of the field on the team’s final possession, ultimately ended in a field goal to take the lead with just over two minutes remaining. The Commanders would drive the field and kick the game-winning field goal on the subsequent possession to send the Bengals to 7-3. Gesicki’s weekly volume remains unlikely to approach elite territory, but his elite red zone usage and penchant for finding paint keeps him in the weekly TE1 discussion in the high-powered Cincinnati offense.

item.title: Samaje Perine rushed six times for 26 yards in the Bengals’ Week 11 loss to the Commanders, adding 71 yards on four receptions.
item.description:
Samaje Perine CIN Running Back

The highlight of the game for Perine came on a 44-yard catch-and-run reception where he chipped into a leak route in the flat, springing free from linebacker coverage to give quarterback Joe Burrow an outlet in the face of pressure. He would outrun the secondary and pick up a key block from fellow running back Chase Brown as he sprung free down the sideline for the longest reception in the game. Perine’s 10 opportunities still ranked below the 14 of Brown but the former handily outproduced the presumed starter on his way to a usable fantasy outing. Up next are the ground-funnel Saints, where Perine will return to shaky Flex status in fantasy circles.

item.title: Chase Brown rushed six times for six yards in the Bengals’ Week 11 loss to the Commanders, adding 30 yards on five receptions.
item.description:
Chase Brown CIN Running Back

Brown saw minimal usage in the first half as the two teams played through driving rain, likely equal parts known tendencies as it was matchup-based. The bigger story here was the involvement of Samaje Perine, who did more than his standard change of pace role implied on his way to 97 total yards. There was no mention of injury or anything that would suggest Brown’s role was limited by necessity, likely best viewed as a small blip on the fantasy radar. Brown’s next opportunity to return a usable fantasy week comes in Week 12 against the Saints, where he will remain a fantasy RB2.

item.title: Joe Burrow completed 28-of-40 passes for 300 yards and two touchdowns in the Bengals’ 22-20, Week 11 loss to the Commanders.
item.description:
Joe Burrow CIN Quarterback

Burrow snapped a steak of five consecutive games in which he accounted for four or more touchdowns in the loss. He came into the game tied for the NFL record for consecutive games with four more touchdowns, ultimately unable to move into sole possession in game that played through driving rain throughout the first half. He leaned heavily on his running backs and tight ends against an aggressive Washington defense, feeding the two positions 24 targets on the evening. A defense that was able to stifle the Commanders in the first half allowed five consecutive scoring drives after the break, all of which were field goals, proving enough to send the Bengals to their third loss of the season. Now 7-3 and only one game ahead of the Browns and Steelers, the Bengals suddenly find themselves locked in one of the tighter divisional battles heading into the final two months of the regular season. Up next for Burrow and the Bengals are the Saints in Week 12, where Burrow will remain a top tier QB1.

item.title: Roschon Johnson (ankle) was listed as a “DNP” on Monday’s estimated practice report.
item.description:
Roschon Johnson CHI Running Back

Johnson departed the team’s Week 11 win over the Saints with an ankle injury and did not return, making his absence Monday notable on the short week. Expect D’Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai to dominate snaps and opportunities out of the backfield for the Bears in one of the biggest games of the season, with the winner left standing alone atop the competitive NFC North.

item.title: Sam LaPorta (ankle) was listed as limited on Monday’s estimated practice report.
item.description:
Sam LaPorta DET Tight End

The ankle appears to be a non-issue, assuming LaPorta can manage to participate in practice Tuesday. The team will hold two more sessions ahead of Thursday’s divisional showdown against the Bears on Thanksgiving, a game that will decide which team stands alone atop the competitive NFC North with six weeks remaining in the regular season.

item.title: Sam Darnold (quad/rib) was present at practice Monday.
item.description:
Sam Darnold SEA Quarterback

The Seahawks held their “bonus” practice Monday as they prepare to face the 49ers on the road in Week 12. The level of participation of Darnold is not fully known considering the team does not owe a full practice report until Wednesday, but Darnold’s presence at practice appears to reinforce previous reports that the team expects him to return following their bye. A potential return would be a sizable boost to alpha wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba.

item.title: Commanders declared CB Amik Robertson, QB Athan Kaliakmanis, RB Robert Henry Jr., Ricky Barber, and G Tanoa Togiai inactive for Week 11 against the Bengals.
item.description:
Ricky Barber WAS Defensive Tackle

The Commanders host one of the league’s hottest teams as they look to avoid falling further behind in the NFC East. They’ll need their defense to step up against a Bengals team averaging 36.2 points per game during their current five-game win streak.

item.title: Bengals declared S Kyle Dugger, OL Myles Hinton, DL Landon Robinson, OL Dalton Risner, and TE Cam Grandy inactive for Week 11 against the Commanders.
item.description:
Kyle Dugger CIN Safety

No real surprises here as the Bengals look to continue their string of recent offensive production against an inferior Washington defense. Joe Burrow gets his full compliment of offensive skill position players minus Andre Iosivas, who remains on injured reserve through Week 11.

item.title: Jake Ferguson was listed as a “DNP” on the estimated practice report Monday.
item.description:
Jake Ferguson DAL Tight End

Even though the team held a walkthrough ahead of their Thanksgiving matchup against the Eagles, the fact that Ferguson has yet to practice after injuring his ankle two weeks ago spells trouble for his potential availability in Week 12. Brevyn Spann-Ford and Luke Schoonmaker appear to be looking at another game atop the depth chart, with volume through the air most likely to concentrate further on CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens.

item.title: Seahawks placed RB George Holani (knee) on injured reserve.
item.description:
George Holani SEA Running Back

The move hurts far less than it would have earlier in the season when both Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price were unavailable. The change of pace option and special teams ace will now miss the next four games, at minimum, placing him in line to potentially return for Week 16 as the Seahawks make their final push toward the postseason.

item.title: Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) was listed as limited on Monday’s estimated injury report.
item.description:
Dalton Kincaid BUF Tight End

Kincaid missed Week 11’s game against the Dolphins with the same set of injuries despite being questionable entering the weekend. It’s quite possible the decision to sit him against the one-win Dolphins was more of a precautionary one ahead of the Bills’ Week 12 matchup against the Chiefs. We’ll see how the rest of his week unfolds, but Kincaid practicing in any capacity this week should be viewed as a good sign for his availability.

Source: Buffalo Bills

item.title: Micah Parson has been cleared to return for the Packers’ Week 12 game against the Rams.
item.description:
Micah Parsons GB Defensive End

This one game a bit earlier than expected. While the hope was Parsons would return on Wednesday, the star pass rusher was listed as a limited participant in Monday’s practice, leaving some doubt as to whether or not he would be cleared for a return. Now, the Packers get back their 2025 sack leader who last played in Week 15 of last season, when he suffered a torn ACL on the road against the Broncos. Parsons will provide an immediate boost to a defense that currently ranks 16th in points allowed but eighth in passing yards allowed per game. They are also tied for the seventh-most team sacks in the league (29), and should see that number creep up a bit with Parsons back in the mix.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Kenneth Walker (groin) was listed as DNP on Monday’s estimated injury report.
item.description:
Kenneth Walker KC Running Back

This wasn’t the news fantasy managers were looking for after going without Walker for each of the last two weeks. The Chiefs’ RB1 has been sidelined with a groin injury he suffered ahead of Week 10’s game against the Falcons, but there was early hope it would be a one-game absence. It was widely believed the decision to sit him against the woeful Cardinals was made to give him additional time to heal up before Week 12’s game against the Bills, but Monday’s DNP now draws his availability against Buffalo into question. The Chiefs didn’t officially practice today, but Walker would not have been present if they did. If he can’t get on the field in even a limited capacity on Tuesday, it would be fair to say he’s trending in the wrong direction ahead of Thursday’s marquee matchup. If Walker is unable to play, Emmett Johnson would be a fringe RB1 after strong performances in back-to-back weeks.

Source: Kansas City Chiefs

item.title: Daniel Jones has cleared waivers and is now free to sign with any team.
item.description:
Daniel Jones

Now that he has passed through waivers, Jones is officially a free agent and is free to sign with any team. While plenty of QB-needy teams could reach out for his services, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported early Monday that Jones will likely wait to sign with a new team and may leave the door open to signing with a contender later in the season that suddenly finds itself in need of a starting QB.

Source: Tom Pelissero

item.title: Quinyon Mitchell (hamstring) did not practice on Monday.
item.description:
Quinyon Mitchell PHI Cornerback

It was an estimated session. Mitchell talked with reporters after leaving Sunday’s game with the hamstring ailment, implying it wasn’t a super serious injury. Still, on a short week, his status is up in the air. If he were ruled out, it would only help CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens on Thanksgiving.

item.title: Broncos designated Tyler Badie (thumb) to return from injured reserve.
item.description:
Tyler Badie DEN Running Back

His 21-day window opens. Seems like perhaps J.K. Dobbins’ suspension has accelerated the timeline on this decision, so Badie may have a chance to be activated for Friday’s game against the Steelers.

item.title: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) is practicing in full ahead of Philadelphia’s Thursday game against the Cowboys.
item.description:
DeVonta Smith PHI Wide Receiver

We’re expecting the Eagles to force-feed Smith once more after his 57 percent target share on Sunday, leaving him as a plausible WR2 in an elevated matchup against the Cowboys defense.

item.title: Will Shipley (foot/illness) was limited in Monday’s practice.
item.description:
Will Shipley PHI Running Back

It was an estimated session and exactly the same listing he had on Friday. As he was practicing on a limited basis before the illness (and before being activated off injured reserve last Saturday), we’ll assume he has a fairly good chance to suit up on Thursday.

item.title: Dallas Goedert (shin) was limited in Monday’s practice.
item.description:
Dallas Goedert PHI Tight End

It’s a new (estimated) listing after his one-catch outing against the Steelers. Goedert was at least set up with a Joe Milton #RevengeGame script against a weak Cowboys defense this week to try to rebound, but it will be hard to rely on him as a streamer TE1 if healthy. We’ll see if he can get to the second part of that statement tomorrow.

item.title: Saquon Barkley (neck/illness) was limited in Monday’s practice.
item.description:
Saquon Barkley PHI Running Back

We described Barkley as leaving the game in the fourth quarter with what “appeared to be a left arm” injury in Sunday’s blurb, it sounds like it may have been a stinger based on the neck listing. A limited (estimated) session is better than a DNP, but Tuesday’s report will loom large for Barkley’s chances of playing against the Cowboys on Thursday.

item.title: Micah Parsons (knee) was limited in Monday’s practice.
item.description:
Micah Parsons GB Defensive End

Parsons has been limited in each of the Packers’ first two practices to start the week. It’s long been believed that the star pass-rusher could be activated for Wednesday’s game against the Rams, but the team has declined to say whether or not that will come to fruition. We will likely have an official word on Parsons’ Week 12 availability when the Packers release their final injury report on Tuesday.

Source: Matt Schneidman

item.title: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports Greg Newsome (ankle) will miss 4-6 weeks.
item.description:
Greg Newsome NYG Cornerback

Newsome will undergo surgery after sustaining a high ankle sprain in Week 11. His absence could be a blow to a Giants secondary that has played well in 2026, allowing the NFL’s 12th lowest drop back success rate and 11th lowest drop back EPA. Newsome through Week 11 had allowed the lowest EPA per target of any Giants cornerback.

Source: Jordan Schultz

item.title: Dallas Goedert (shin) was listed as a limited participant on Monday’s estimated practice report.
item.description:
Dallas Goedert PHI Tight End

Likely nothing to see here as the veteran tight end prepares for a divisional matchup against the Cowboys on Thanksgiving. Goedert’s 38-yard reception last week against the Steelers was his longer catch since Week 1, although the fact it was his only grab is troubling considering it was the first game with a healthy DeVonta Smith in a month. Goedert has been relegated to a top end TE2 against the Cowboys.

item.title: Saquon Barkley (neck/illness) was listed as a limited participant on Monday’s estimated practice report.
item.description:
Saquon Barkley PHI Running Back

Barkley should be good to go for the team’s Thanksgiving showdown against the Cowboys Thursday despite the dual-tag designation. The veteran workhorse is coming off one of his best performances of the season against the Steelers, leading the team to their first win in two calendar months.

item.title: Colby Parkinson (ribs) practiced in full on Monday.
item.description:
Colby Parkinson

He’s gotten in two full sessions coming off the bye and figures to remain one of the main figures in the Rams’ floating opera of tight end production that they’ll likely be relying on this week sans Puka Nacua and Davante Adams.

item.title: Josh Jacobs (thumb) was limited in Monday’s practice.
item.description:
Josh Jacobs GB Running Back

Jacobs has been limited in each of the Packers’ first two practices as they prepare to face the Rams on Wednesday. While a limited session would generally be viewed as an encouraging sign for a player, head coach Matt LaFleur said earlier that he doesn’t expect Jacobs to suit up this week. We will continue to track his status until he receives an official designation for the game, but we’re assuming based on LaFleur’s comments that Jacobs will miss at least one more week.

Source: Matt Schneidman

item.title: Kyren Williams (toe) practiced in full on Monday.
item.description:
Kyren Williams

It’s an upgrade from a limited session on Sunday and we’d be surprised if Williams was placed on the questionable line on Tuesday.

item.title: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports DK Metcalf will not be suspended following his ejection from Week 11’s game against the Eagles.
item.description:
DK Metcalf PIT Wide Receiver

Metcalf allegedly tried to poke Eagles CB Cooper DeJean in the eye during an altercation. While Metcalf denies those allegations, whatever he was attempting to do certainly didn’t look good on tape. While the league has opted not to suspend Metcalf for his actions, he could still face fines for his conduct, which would be handed down later in the week. That said, Metcalf should be good to go for Week 12’s game against the Broncos.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: Commanders activated RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) off injured reserve.
item.description:
Jacory Croskey-Merritt WAS Running Back

“Bill” has missed the minimum four games and was designated as questionable; he has been removed from the injury report by the Commanders and should be their lead back. You likely already had plans to start him if you were holding up your FLEX spot or RB2 position for him, and now you officially can do so.

item.title: Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell said he doesn’t “necessarily expect to have Jordan Addison (thumb)” back for Week 12 against the Falcons.
item.description:
Jordan Addison MIN Wide Receiver

Addison underwent thumb surgery last week after suffering what was described as a “freak injury” in practice. While he wasn’t considered a candidate for injured reserve, O’Connell did say after the injury that he would likely miss multiple games before returning. If Addison is unable to play in Week 12, it would be the third straight game he has missed with the injury. His practice status will be one to monitor throughout the week.

Source: Kevin Seifert

item.title: The Denver Post’s Parker Gabriel reports RJ Harvey (IR/knee) is “widely expected” to practice when first eligible to come off injured reserve.
item.description:
RJ Harvey DEN Running Back

Harvey will miss Black Friday’s game against the Steelers, but it sounds like that might be the last one he misses. Jonah Coleman has established a fiefdom at the top of the depth chart in Harvey’s absence, so the second-year back doesn’t necessarily return to a major role in Week 13, but he may be worth picking up in deeper leagues if he was dropped.

Source: Denver Post

item.title: Giants head coach John Harbaugh said CB Greg Newsome will miss multiple weeks with a high-ankle sprain.
item.description:
Greg Newsome NYG Cornerback

Newsome’s injury comes just weeks after he signed a three-year, $46 million contract extension with the Giants. The 26-year-old corner has appeared on 483 defensive snaps this season, earning a PFF coverage grade of 71.2 while allowing opposing receivers to catch 19 passes for 209 scoreless yards. His absence will be a tough blow to a Giants secondary that ranks fourth in net yards allowed per attempt and fifth in overall passing yards allowed this season.

Source: Charlotte Carroll

item.title: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said he is “very confident” Michael Pittman (foot) will play in Week 12 against the Broncos.
item.description:
Michael Pittman PIT Wide Receiver

Pittman hasn’t played since Week 4 and has put together a forgettable 7-89-0 line in the three games he has suited up for this season. His return comes as the Steelers are in the midst of an offensive slump, as they’ve averaged just 19.3 points per game in their last four games while going 1-3. They’ll need all hands on deck as they prepare to face a tough Broncos defense on Friday.

Source: Brooke Pryor

item.title: Rams head coach Sean McVay said Terrance Ferguson will undergo season-ending ankle surgery.
item.description:
Terrance Ferguson

Ferguson tried multiple times to make his way back from the ankle injury that has sidelined him since Week 3. Initially expected to return in Week 9, Ferguson suffered a hamstring injury in practice that further delayed his return, but it doesn’t sound like his ankle ever fully healed in light of today’s news. Ferguson’s season comes to an end after just three games. The second-year tight end turned in an impressive 6-54-1 line in Week 2 against the Giants, but saw just three targets over his other two games. The former second-round pick is an explosive playmaker with the ball in his hand and could make for an intriguing late-round pick in fantasy leagues next year once healthy.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: NBC Houston’s Aaron Wilson reports Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) is dealing with a short-term strain.
item.description:
Marvin Harrison HOU Wide Receiver

Danielle Hunter, too, is dealing with one of these. It seems like after the lengthy layoff following Thursday night’s win over the Colts, the Texans could be in line to get both players back for Week 12’s game against the Ravens.

Source: Aaron Wilson

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Commanders are Brandon Aiyuk’s “most likely” landing spot.
item.description:
Brandon Aiyuk

The ink on the release wasn’t even given time to dry before Aiyuk was connected to the same team he was connected to all offseason. He’ll likely wind up with a spot on the Commanders practice squad. Given the lengthy layoff, we probably don’t need to imagine Aiyuk suiting up in Week 12 as a destined outcome, but it could be sooner rather than later.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: 49ers released WR Brandon Aiyuk.
item.description:
Brandon Aiyuk

Took them long enough, you might say before you were pedanted by those who would tell you things like “Aiyuk had to report to actually be released.” It should be noted that Aiyuk must clear waivers since this is after the trade deadline, but nobody is expected to assume his contract. Anyway, Aiyuk will be free to pursue free agency and it sounds like we have another blurb to write about that almost instantly, funny how that works. The 28-year-old will look to continue his career elsewhere, perhaps somewhere in the greater Washington D.C. area.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Chiefs OC Eric Bieniemy said Kenneth Walker (groin) will “remain the starter” when he returns.
item.description:
Kenneth Walker KC Running Back

Rookie Emmett Johnson has rushed for 45-206-1 in two games without Walker this season, which has led some to wonder what role Walker could have when he returns from his groin injury. Walker, who currently ranks fifth in the league in rushing yards (872) and leads the league in yards per carry (5.5) could return as early as this Thursday when the Bills play host to the Chiefs on Thanksgiving, and from the sound of things, it would be safe to say he will be in line for plenty of work. Speaking Monday with the media, Bieniemy said that while Johnson has been impressive in his two games as a starter, the Chiefs “also understand the value [Walker] brings as well.” His practice status will be one to monitor this week, but if he’s active, Walker would be an easy must-start in what could be a high-scoring affair.

Source: Charles Goldman

item.title: FOX Sports’ Jay Glazer reports the 49ers signed President of Football Operations and GM John Lynch to an extension.
item.description:
John Lynch SF General Manager

Lynch joined the Niners as general manager in 2017 and was promoted to President of Football Operations in 2023. Since his arrival, the Niners have emerged as one of the better-run organizations in the league. Under Lynch, the Niners have gone 91-68 in the regular season while making two trips to the Super Bowl and four trips to the NFC Championship Game. His selection of Brock Purdy as the final pick of the 2022 NFL Draft ended up giving head coach Kyle Shanahan his long-term QB of the future after previously failed attempts to address the position post Alex Smith and Colin Kaepernick, and in a season where the Niners have been dealt multiple injuries, specifically at receiver, San Francisco currently finds itself with a 9-1 record and three games ahead of the Seahawks and Rams in the NFC West. It’s a much-deserved extension for Lynch, who again has his team on track to make a deep run in the postseason.

Source: Jay Glazer

item.title: Panthers coach Dave Canales said Jalen Coker has cleared concussion protocol.
item.description:
Jalen Coker CAR Wide Receiver

Coker was checked in the fourth quarter after taking a hard hit from Roquan Smith, but it looks like he’ll be fine to use against the Buccaneers on Monday night. With all 32 teams active, it may be time to capitulate and put Coker back on the WR3 line. He has not cleared 50 yards since Week 6.

Source: Mike Kaye

item.title: Panthers coach Dave Canales said Trevor Etienne’s production and Tre Tyus’ special teams value make it “challenging” to find a spot for Jonathon Brooks.
item.description:
Jonathon Brooks CAR Running Back

Brooks, who is on injured reserve due to a groin injury, has eight days to be activated or lost for the season. The 23-year-old back practiced in full last week all three times only to not be activated. It would be great news for Chuba Hubbard if this continued, as the team has shown little interest in using Etienne in a real role in the backfield.

Source: Joe Person

item.title: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said Josh Jacobs (finger) is unlikely to play in Week 12 against the Rams.
item.description:
Josh Jacobs GB Running Back

Jacobs was listed as limited in Sunday’s practice as the Packers prepare to take on the Rams on Wednesday, but he’s still only nine days removed from the surgery to repair his fractured ring finger. It was reported shortly after his injury that Jacobs could miss 2-3 weeks, and a return in Week 13 would put him close to that three-week timetable. It doesn’t sound like we should expect to see him this week against the Rams, but a return against the Saints could be in the cards if all goes well.

Source: Rob Demovsky

item.title: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said “Tommy [DeVito is] our starter” when asked if the team plans to add a QB in the coming days.
item.description:
Tommy DeVito NE Quarterback

After news broke last week of Drake Maye’s injury and impending absence of six-plus weeks, it was reported that the Patriots could explore QB options outside the building to take over for the Pats’ QB1. The recent release of Daniel Jones by the Colts makes that subject all the more interesting, but Vrabel, at least for now, seems committed to 28-year-old DeVito, who is set to make his first start as a Patriot in Week 12 against the Chargers. Vrabel praised DeVito for the improved play he showed in training camp and the preseason and expressed confidence in him to lead the offense and run the huddle. DeVito hasn’t started a game since the 2024 season with the Giants and has a career passing line of 1,490-9-4 in 15 career games. He threw for 81 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in relief if Maye in Week 10, but will be hard to trust as anything more than a desperation play in 2QB/Superflex leagues next week against the Chargers.

Source: Mass Live

item.title: Cardinals fired DC Nick Rallis.
item.description:
Nick Rallis

Rallis, whose unit had allowed 323 points in 11 weeks, more than anyone but the Raiders, will give way to interim DC Teryl Austin. Still just 33, there’s a chance the ultra-aggressive Rallis will get another opportunity in this post down the line. Weirdly, the defense hasn’t been the No. 1 problem area in Arizona lately — though that’s certainly more about quarterback attrition than anything — but it’s hard to say that Rallis ever produced a notably above-average unit in three-and-a-half years in the desert. The Cardinals best finish over that span was 14th in DVOA in 2024.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Jaguars coach Liam Coen said Bhayshul Tuten (ankle) re-aggravated his injury against the Giants and it will be “business as usual” with him in practice this week.
item.description:
Bhayshul Tuten

In other words, look for a lot of DNPs and limited sessions that don’t really matter, then a Friday decision at the end of the week. The Jaguars certainly could decide they have the luxury of resting Tuten against the Titans in Week 12. Chris Rodriguez could be either a viable RB2 or a useless FLEX play by Friday, depending on how this situation shakes out.

Source: Mia O’Brien

item.title: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Seth McGowan (hamstring) “will miss some time.”
item.description:
Seth McGowan IND Running Back

McGowan exited in Week 11’s loss to the Texans and did not return to the game. The rookie seventh-rounder had been seeing an increased role as of late, rushing 26 times for 158 yards and two touchdowns in his last four games while adding two receptions. His absence should create a slight uptick in opportunities for Jonathan Taylor, who has had no more than 16 rush attempts in his last four games. We’ll likely get a better sense of how long McGowan could be out in the coming days, but for now, DJ Giddens appears next in line behind Taylor.

Source: James Boyd

item.title: Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said “as of today” Malik Willis’ groin injury will not require surgery.
item.description:
Malik Willis MIA Quarterback

It sounds like this is subject to change, as Hafley also added that Willis will “be re-evaluated at the four-week mark” of his absence to see where things stand. Willis has already spent two weeks on injured reserve and will need to miss at least two more games before the Dolphins could consider bringing him back in Week 14 against the Bears. Kyle McCord has struggled in his two starts, completing 44.6 percent of his passes while throwing for 311-0-1, and will be under center again in Week 12 against the Jets.

Source: Barry Jackson

item.title: Ja’Kobi Lane was not targeted in the Ravens’ Week 11 loss to the Panthers.
item.description:
Ja'Kobi Lane BAL Wide Receiver

After seeing a season-high 11 targets in Week 10’s loss to the Chargers, Lane went on to donut in Sunday’s loss to the Panthers. The rookie’s lack of targets wasn’t due to a shortage of playing time, as his 23 routes run were good for third most of any Ravens receiver, but the ball simply wasn’t finding him. With all 32 teams playing in Week 12, fantasy managers shouldn’t trust Lane in any capacity next week against the Texans.

item.title: Darren Waller caught 3-of-3 targets for 42 yards in the Panthers’ Week 11 win over the Ravens.
item.description:
Darren Waller CAR Tight End

Waller’s biggest play came on a 27-yard reception in the third quarter. He caught one of three deep balls from Bryce Young, but fellow tight end Mitchell Evans outperformed him, posting a 5-44-1 line in what turned out to be a career day for the third-year tight end. Waller won’t be anything more than a boom-or-bust TE2 in Week 12 against the Buccaneers.

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said Daniel Jones could wait to sign with a new team if he goes unclaimed on waivers.
item.description:
Daniel Jones

The belief is that Jones won’t be claimed on waivers, since any team that claims him would inherit his remaining contract with the Colts. Instead, Jones will likely pass through waivers and become a free agent, but he could delay signing with a new team immediately and instead opt to wait and see what other options may become available during the season. As Rapoport pointed out on Monday on NFL Network’s Good Morning Football, “someone, some playoff-ready team unfortunately is going to lose a quarterback at some point,” which could open the door for Jones to join a legitimate contender over the final stretch of the season and ahead of the playoffs. It was reported earlier that the Patriots and Ravens could be interested in Jones, but both teams would be on the outside looking in if the postseason began today. Jones struggled mightily in his second season with the Colts, throwing for 1,974-7-13 in 11 games, but he would likely be an upgrade over several teams’ backup QBs if a starter goes down.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports 49ers RT Colton McKivitz will likely miss the remainder of the season after suffering fracturing and dislocating his ankle in Week 11’s win over the Vikings.
item.description:
Colton McKivitz SF Offensive Lineman

If you saw this injury during the game, you immediately knew this would likely be a season-ender. McKivitz’s left leg twisted unnaturally after a play in the second quarter, and the 30-year-old tackle was carted off the field shortly after. While we hope for the best, we fully expect the team to announce McKivitz’s season is over at some point this week. McKivitz was replaced by Vederian Lowe, who will presumably be the Niners’ starting right tackle moving forward.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports DK Metcalf’s actions will be “reviewed for potential additional discipline, including suspension” following his ejection in Week 11 against the Eagles.
item.description:
DK Metcalf PIT Wide Receiver

Metcalf was ejected from Sunday’s game against the Eagles after receiving his second unsportsmanlike conduct penalty. The 28-year-old receiver ended the day with one catch for two yards and had two altercations with Eagles CB Cooper DeJean before he was sent to the locker room. Metcalf will almost certainly receive a fine from the league in the coming days, but a suspension could put him in line to miss Week 12’s game against the Broncos.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Deebo Samuel caught 3-of-4 targets for 20 yards in the 49ers’ Week 11 win over the Vikings, adding 27 yards on two carries.
item.description:
Deebo Samuel SF Wide Receiver

Samuel continued to operate as the primary gadget player for a 49ers team now with Christian McCaffrey, Mike Evans, and George Kittle all fully healthy. While that role carries per-touch upside given the space he should have when receiving the ball, fantasy managers are likely forced to view Samuel more as a potential Flex than a viable weekly starter. That will remain true ahead of a Week 12 meeting with the Seahawks.

item.title: George Kittle caught all three passes for 34 yards and two touchdowns in the 49ers’ Week 11 win over the Vikings.
item.description:
George Kittle SF Tight End

Kittle got to work early, capping off the opening drive with a touchdown from 17 yards out before adding a second touchdown early in the second quarter. The team would score again on their subsequent possession before the defense tacked on a pick-six on the following play, capping passing volume and leading to the low target total for the veteran tight end in the process. Even so, Kittle continued to showcase his elite athleticism, body control, and strength on his two scores and remains a surefire TE1 heading into another difficult matchup against the Seahawks in Week 12.

item.title: Keenan Allen caught 3-of-4 targets for 38 yards in the 49ers’ Week 11 win over the Vikings.
item.description:
Keenan Allen SF Wide Receiver

Allen was hardly used in the first half as George Kittle and Mike Evans did all the heavy lifting but came alive in the third quarter to get his name in the box score. The 49ers’ most recent addition provides yet another offensive weapon alongside Evans, Kittle, Christian McCaffrey, and Deebo Samuel, all of whom are now healthy as the team continues its press toward the only bye out of the NFC. Allen will be a difficult start in fantasy with the other supporting cast fully healthy as they prepare to face the Seahawks in Week 12.

item.title: Mike Evans caught 6-of-7 targets for 109 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 11 win over the Vikings.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

Fantasy managers took a collective sigh of relief after Evans was shown on the sideline grimacing in the first quarter. The team would never pass an injury update for their veteran star, who would later connect with quarterback Brock Purdy in the second quarter from four yards out to push the team’s lead to 21-10. The defense would step up with a pick-six on Minnesota’s subsequent possession, allowing the 49ers to coast to the win in the second half. As is typically the case, Evans caught numerous key passes on third down to extend drives, using his large frame to great effect on both slants and on the perimeter. His touchdown was a fade to the corner of the end zone, highlighting the full range of his talents against a formidable opponent. Fantasy managers will want to track his practice availability in the coming days, but it appears likely Evans can be inserted into lineups as a viable WR1 when the 49ers take on the Seahawks in Week 12.

item.title: Christian McCaffrey rushed 12 times for 49 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 11 win over the Vikings, adding 13 yards on two receptions.
item.description:
Christian McCaffrey SF Running Back

McCaffrey found the end zone for the 14th time this season, marking his ninth consecutive game with a touchdown after failing to find paint in Week 1 against the Rams in Australia. The modest carry total and receiving total were more a comment on how much of a stranglehold the 49ers had on the game than anything else, coasting in the second half after jumping out to a 28-10 lead in the second quarter. The starters would then rest for the team’s final two possessions following McCaffrey’s fourth quarter touchdown. McCaffrey remains an elite RB1 ahead of a Week 12 meeting with the division rival Seahawks.

item.title: Brock Purdy completed 21-of-26 passes for 255 yards and three touchdowns in the 49ers’ 35-10, Week 11 win over the Vikings.
item.description:
Brock Purdy SF Quarterback

Purdy and the 49ers controlled the tempo throughout against the aggressive Minnesota defense, expertly handling the blitz as the 49ers jumped out to a 21-10 lead in the second quarter by finding paint on three of their first four possessions. The lead was extended on a pick-six shortly thereafter, allowing the 49ers to coast to their ninth victory of the season. The team now has a stranglehold on the once-competitive NFC West and the inside track to the only bye out of the conference, with only the four teams in the NFC North threatening that claim. The former Mr. Irrelevant tossed three touchdowns for the second consecutive game and the fourth time this season, keeping him in the QB1 ranks in fantasy ahead of another stiff test against the Seahawks in Week 12.

item.title: Jauan Jennings caught 3-of-6 targets for 20 yards in the Vikings’ Week 11 loss to the 49ers.
item.description:
Jauan Jennings MIN Wide Receiver

Jennings operated in a familiar WR3 role for the Vikings despite the absence of Jordan Addison, with Tai Felton getting the start on the perimeter opposite Justin Jefferson. Fantasy managers that thought they were pulling a fast one by adding Jennings are likely better off scooping Felton as a viable Flex for as long as Addison remains sidelined.

item.title: Tai Felton caught 6-of-12 targets for 42 yards in the Vikings’ Week 11 loss to the 49ers.
item.description:
Tai Felton MIN Wide Receiver

Felton operated as a starter on the perimeter opposite Justin Jefferson but was unable to capitalize on a team-leading 12 targets. Even so, Felton should be expected to continue as a starter in the offense for as long as Jordan Addison remains sidelined due to a thumb injury, a role that could yield viable Flex status in the coming weeks. Fantasy managers in a bind could do worse than scooping Felton from waivers ahead of a Week 12 meeting with the Falcons.

item.title: T.J. Hockenson caught 6-of-7 targets for 55 yards in the Vikings’ Week 11 loss to the 49ers.
item.description:
T.J. Hockenson MIN Tight End

The highlight of the game for the veteran tight end was a posterizing catch down the sideline for a 20-yard gain on the team’s opening possession, a drive that resulted in the first of two missed field goal attempts. Hockenson would play the role of Mr. Reliable from that point forward, although his seven targets finished third on the team behind Justin Jefferson and Tai Felton. The Vikings get the 3-7 Falcons at home in Week 12, where Hockenson will remain a volume-driven TE1.

item.title: Justin Jefferson caught 7-of-9 targets for 86 yards in the Vikings’ Week 11 loss to the 49ers, adding one yard on one carry.
item.description:
Justin Jefferson MIN Wide Receiver

Kirk Cousins and Kevin O’Connell did what they could to get Jefferson involved early and often, although his nine targets ended second on the team behind Tai Felton’s 12. His lone mistake in the game was a costly one, with Jefferson losing a fumble with the team driving on their first possession of the second half down 28-10. The team would not recover after the untimely error, failing to add additional scoring while turning the ball over twice on downs during their subsequent three possessions. Jefferson is clearly in better hands with Cousins under center, a situation that should hold moving forward despite the veteran signal caller being replaced late in a lost game. Fantasy managers can start Jefferson with confidence as an upside WR2 against the Falcons in Week 12.

item.title: Aaron Jones rushed eight times for 30 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings’ Week 11 loss to the 49ers, adding 13 yards on one reception.
item.description:
Aaron Jones MIN Running Back

Jones continues to cede primary rushing duties between the 20s to Jordan Mason but scored for the second consecutive game. After serving as a workhorse back with Mason on the shelf, Jones has not seen more than 11 carries since Mason returned in Week 7, having been held to eight carries or fewer in four of five games. That leaves very little room for fantasy upside on the worse side of a true timeshare, meaning fantasy managers are better off leaving Jones on their bench ahead of a Week 12 meeting with the Falcons.

item.title: Jordan Mason rushed 11 times for 38 yards in the Vikings’ Week 11 loss to the 49ers, losing one yard on one reception.
item.description:
Jordan Mason MIN Running Back

Mason led the team in rush attempts and yardage while ceding high-value touches to Aaron Jones for the second consecutive week, with the latter accounting for the only touchdown scored by the Vikings in the loss. The poor game environment and inability of the offense to sustain drives led to the modest touch total for the veteran back, who has become a difficult player to trust in fantasy circles given the current split in workload. Fantasy managers likely have better options ahead of a Week 12 meeting with the Falcons.

item.title: Kirk Cousins completed 26-of-38 passes for 235 yards and one interception in the Vikings’ 35-10, Week 11 loss to the 49ers.
item.description:
Kirk Cousins MIN Quarterback

This one started with all the makings of a true shootout, with the two teams trading blows early to push the score to 14-10 in favor of the 49ers through the first six possessions. That would be where the offensive production stopped for the Vikings, who turned the ball over twice and missed two field goals. We’ll give a pass on the second field goal attempt missed considering it came up just feet short of setting a new NFL record at 71 yards in the altitude in Mexico. The tires became entirely deflated for the Vikings after a Justin Jefferson fumble halted any momentum coming out of the half while trailing 28-10. A touchdown on that drive makes it a game, but the Vikings ultimately failed to muster any additional scoring after their third possession of the game. Cousins ended up giving way to Carson Wentz in the fourth quarter in a lost game after failing to throw for a touchdown for the first time this season. The 7-3 Vikings get a full week to prepare for the Falcons in Week 12, where Cousins will return as an upside QB2.

item.title: Jaylen Waddle caught 3-of-6 targets for 61 yards in the Broncos’ Week 11 win over the Raiders.
item.description:
Jaylen Waddle DEN Wide Receiver

Sean Payton tried to get Waddle going as a deep option today with mixed results. Waddle gained at least 18 yards on all three of his catches. He was also held to just three catches. Waddle has caught more than five passes in one game this year. Today was just his second outing over 50 yards. Waddle isn’t completely useless for fantasy purposes, but the case for him as a WR3 grows worse by the week. With no teams on bye in Week 12, Waddle will finally hit the WR4 ranks versus Pittsburgh.

item.title: Courtland Sutton did not catch either of his targets in the Broncos’ Week 11 win over the Raiders.
item.description:
Courtland Sutton DEN Wide Receiver

Sutton posted a solid 5-45-1 receiving line before the Broncos’ Week 10 bye, but it felt like the team was ready to move Pat Bryant into a larger role. Bryant only managed four targets, but it was his first time seeing more looks than Sutton all year. He caught three of them for 32 yards. Now facing increased competition for opportunities, Sutton’s fantasy outlook is going from bad to worse headed into Week 12. He will be a touchdown-or-bust WR5 versus the Steelers.

item.title: Jakobi Meyers caught 4-of-10 targets for 84 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 11 loss against the Giants.
item.description:
Jakobi Meyers

Meyers was second on the team in targets and receiving yards, trailing Parker Washington’s eight catches for 103 yards. Meyers’ 26-yard grab was the biggest play of the day for the Jaguars, who were forced into a pass-heavy chase script in the second half — a rarity for Jacksonville. Meyers will be a passable WR3 play in Week 12 against the Titans. He had 34 yards on three catches against the Titans in Week 10.

item.title: Pat Bryant caught 3-of-4 targets for 32 yards in the Broncos’ Week 11 win over the Raiders.
item.description:
Pat Bryant DEN Wide Receiver

Bryant got off to a hot start with a 20-yard grab on the Broncos’ opening drive. That would account for over half of his production on the day as Bo Nix could not get any of his receivers going. Bryant still finished second among the team’s wideouts in targets, though Evan Engram and Jonah Coleman both saw more opportunities in the passing game than him. Bryant also survived an injury scare late in the game. His leg got rolled on during a tackle in the fourth quarter. He tried to get up but went back down on the field. Bryant walked off under his own power, worked through the issue on the sideline, and returned a few plays later. We expect to see him on the injury report, but he should be available for Week 12. He will be in the WR4 mix versus Pittsburgh.

item.title: Chris Rodriguez had four rushes for 28 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 11 loss to the Giants, adding one catch for 13 yards.
item.description:
Chris Rodriguez

C-Rod handled a limited workload again, even despite Bhayshul Tuten coming on and off the field with ankle and knee injuries that have slowed him down of late. Tuten ended the game with ten carries and three receptions. Rodriguez could have a valuable workload in Week 12 against the Titans if the Jaguars rest Tuten for the stretch run. Rodriguez should be rostered in all formats as a solid contingency option.

item.title: Evan Engram caught 6-of-8 targets for 74 yards in the Broncos’ Week 11 win over the Raiders.
item.description:
Evan Engram DEN Tight End

Engram was surprisingly involved in this game, and not just on check-downs. Four of his catches went for at least 10 yards, propelling him to a season-high in receiving yards. The only downside to his performance was the lack of a touchdown. That went to Adam Trautman on a short goal-line toss. While Engram’s pop-up game might help some best ball players, it’s not worth chasing headed into Week 12 against the Steelers.

item.title: Josh Cameron caught 3-of-7 targets for 44 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 11 loss to the Giants.
item.description:
Josh Cameron

Cameron ran only 22 routes on 56 Jacksonville drop backs but was second behind only Parker Washington (12) in targets. Cameron will be a borderline fantasy option next week against a terrible Titans secondary. Cameron had 67 yards on three catches against Tennessee in Week 10.

item.title: Brian Thomas caught 1-of-3 targets for 18 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 11 loss against the Giants.
item.description:
Brian Thomas

Thomas, who ran a pass route on 33 of the team’s 56 drop backs, caught his first touchdown since Week 8 and only his third score of the year. His route involvement saw a bump over Josh Cameron, who had been playing more than BTJ. Cameron had just 21 routes on the day and caught three balls for 44 yards. Thomas was among the Jacksonville pass catchers who benefited from the game’s inflated volume. He’ll be a high variance flex play in Week 12 against the Colts.

item.title: J.K. Dobbins rushed one time for zero yards in the Broncos’ Week 11 win over the Raiders.
item.description:
J.K. Dobbins DEN Running Back

Jonah Coleman completed his takeover of the backfield today with 24 carries, four catches, and three touchdowns. Dobbins, meanwhile, saw as many carries as Cody Schrader. Dobbins’ carry total has gone from seven to four to one in his past three appearances. Sean Payton has decided that this is Coleman’s backfield and there’s not much Dobbins can do about it. Fantasy managers can cut ties with him on the next run of waivers.

item.title: Bo Nix completed 19-of-35 passes for 225 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Broncos’ 38-24, Week 11 win over the Raiders.
item.description:
Bo Nix DEN Quarterback

Nix got on the board early with a goal line toss to Adam Trautman, but it was all Jonah Coleman after that. The rookie running back punched in three rushing touchdowns, all from no farther than seven yards out. Nix did have several close calls on the day. He threw a well-placed deep ball to Troy Franklin, and the pass simply doinked off his helmet. Franklin was laying out for the ball, so it may not have been a touchdown, but it still would have juiced Nix’s box score. Nix also threw a dime to Marvin Mims on a flea-flicker that went down to the one-yard line. He was then stuffed on a sneak, after which Coleman made it into the end zone. All in, it was a better performance from Nix than the box score suggests. With no teams on bye next week, Nix will likely be relegated to the top of the QB2 ranks for his date with the Steelers.

item.title: Brenton Strange caught all three of his targets for 16 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 11 loss against the Giants.
item.description:
Brenton Strange

Strange didn’t see much involvement in a game that saw Trevor Lawrence attempt a season-high 47 passes, though he ran a route on 44 of the team’s 49 drop backs. Strange, who has more than five targets in five games this season, will be a fine fantasy option in Week 12 against a Colts defense that ranks among the most generous to enemy tight ends.

item.title: Michael Mayer caught 1-of-4 targets for four yards in the Raiders’ Week 11 loss to the Broncos.
item.description:
Michael Mayer LV Tight End

To add insult to injury for fantasy managers who streamed Mayer, Ian Thomas found the end zone on his only grab of the day. Mayer has typically played the inline tight end role with Brock Bowers operating as a de facto wide receiver. Because of that, Bowers’ absence today didn’t actually free up that many extra snaps or routes for Mayer. The targets also went to the team’s wide receivers instead of Mayer. Whether or not Bowers plays next week doesn’t make much of a difference for Mayer. He will be, at best, a low-end TE2.

item.title: JJ McCarthy completed 18-of-38 attempts for 173 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 11 win against the Jaguars, adding seven rushes for 33 yards.
item.description:
J.J. McCarthy NYG Quarterback

McCarthy looked out of sorts from start to finish. He airmailed a few routine throws and made some questionable decisions from the pocket against a stingy Jacksonville defense. He finished the game 15 percent below his expected completion rate and with a negative EPA per drop back. McCarthy fed Malik Nabers, who managed 55 yards on a dozen targets. He should be a decent streaming option in Week 12 against a Colts defense that has been among the league’s worst over the past month, though Jameis Winston’s tush push involvement has negatively impacted McCarthy’s weekly fantasy prospects.

item.title: Kimani Vidal rushed seven times for 36 yards in the Chargers’ Week 11 loss to the Jets, adding two receptions for 18 yards.
item.description:
Kimani Vidal LAC Running Back

Keaton Mitchell’s knee and back injuries allowed Vidal to play a little more often on passing downs. Vidal had a five-yard catch called back due to a penalty, and he was given a carry from the Jets’ eight-yard line. He got open on 2nd-and-goal, a few yards shy of the end zone, late in the game, but Justin Herbert unsuccessfully tried to force a throw to Quentin Johnston in the back of the end zone. Herbert was placed in the NFL’s concussion protocol after the game. Vidal could warrant FLEX consideration against the Patriots next week, but Mitchell and Herbert’s health will factor into things.

item.title: Colton McKivitz (leg) was carted to the locker room in the second quarter of Week 11 against the Vikings.
item.description:
Colton McKivitz SF Offensive Lineman

McKivitz was rolled up on from behind and his leg did things it should not do, with the gruesome injury almost assuredly going to end his season. The veteran right tackle had become a staple for the 49ers before his injury, with the team now forced to shuffle things up front for the remainder of the season. Expect updates from the team in the coming days.

item.title: Jack Bech caught 8-of-9 targets for 89 yards and a touchdown in the Raiders’ Week 11 loss to the Broncos.
item.description:
Jack Bech LV Wide Receiver

Bech quietly led the Raiders with seven targets last week but failed to do anything with the sizable role. Though he came up one target shy of the team lead this time around, Bech was the Raiders’ most productive wide receiver or tight end by a wide margin. Fernando Mendoza consistently found him for chunk gains, with four of his grabs resulting in either a first down or a touchdown. Bech’s second score of the year came on a seven-yard out near the goal line. He was initially ruled down at the one, but an expedited review put him on the board. Bech’s role will take a hit if Brock Bowers is able to play in Week 12, but he’s at least challenging Tre Tucker for the WR1 role. He will be a high-risk FLEX play for his Week 12 game against Cleveland.

item.title: Devin Singletary had one rush for five yards in the Giants’ Week 11 win against the Jaguars, adding one catch for five yards.
item.description:
Devin Singletary NYG Running Back

Singletary was strictly in a breather back role behind Cam Skattebo, who struggled to get anything going against the Jags. Singletary won’t have any fantasy value unless or until Skattebo misses time in the coming weeks.

item.title: Omarion Hampton rushed 14 times for 89 yards in the Chargers’ Week 11 loss to the Jets, adding one reception for four yards.
item.description:
Omarion Hampton LAC Running Back

Hampton ripped off a 30-plus-yard run for the second time in three weeks today, averaging 6.4 yards per carry. He is the Chargers’ best runner, but frequent losing game scripts make his rushing workloads somewhat unreliable. The Chargers called an option run play for Justin Herbert in the red zone late in the game, with Hampton running a couple yards away from him, but Jets defenders recognized it and shut the play down, erasing Hampton’s potential opportunity to catch a pitch and run it in. Keaton Mitchell suffered back and knee injuries and departed early. Justin Herbert entered the NFL’s concussion protocol after the game. Hampton could warrant RB2 treatment against the Patriots next week, but both injuries will impact his projection.

item.title: Cam Skattebo had 14 rushes for 34 yards in the Giants’ Week 11 win against the Jaguars, adding three catches for 14 yards.
item.description:
Cam Skattebo NYG Running Back

It was not the most efficient outing for the backflipping Skattebo, who averaged a meager 2.8 yards per touch and was regularly stuffed at or near the line of scrimmage against a stingy Jacksonville front seven. He did, however, manage 14 of the team’s 15 running back carries. Devin Singletary was limited to one carry on the day. Skattebo will be a solid RB2 option in Week 12 against a Cowboys defense allowing the second highest rate of fantasy points per touch to opposing running backs this season.

item.title: Tre Tucker caught 2-of-10 targets for 50 yards in the Raiders’ Week 11 loss to the Broncos.
item.description:
Tre Tucker LV Wide Receiver

Tucker led the Raiders in targets, though several of his looks were uncatchable. He racked up plenty of prayer yards but didn’t do much in the way of actual receiving production. The bulk of his output came on a 39-yard toss from Fernando Mendoza in the fourth quarter. Jack Bech, on the other hand, went for 88 yards and a score on eight targets.
